class_name: 話題-も観点-トシテモ類

provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

glosses: as X as well; from X's side also
patterns.usage_note: States the named party's own standpoint: X, in its capacity as X, holds this position as well as whoever else does (市としても対応を急いでおります, 私としても賛成だ), usually implying commitment or feeling rather than a bare fact. The sibling にしても・にしたって instead grants a case the listener assumed was exceptional. A clause plus としても is a separate construction meaning "even if"; this entry attaches to nouns.

examples.ruby: 母[はは]としても、私[わたし]の一人[ひとり]暮[ぐ]らしは心配[しんぱい]なのだろう。
examples.english: My mother, for her part, must be worried about me living alone.

examples.ruby: 私[わたし]としても、練習[れんしゅう]は土曜[どよう]のほうがありがたい。
examples.english: For my part too, I'd be glad if practice were on Saturday.

examples.ruby: 学校[がっこう]としましても、給食[きゅうしょく]の見直[みなお]しを進[すす]めております。
examples.english: The school, for its part, is working on a review of the lunch program.

glosses: as far as X is concerned too
patterns.usage_note: Adds X as one more party the same thing is true of: the noun names a further person or side alongside the one under discussion (親にしたって心配なんだ), often pushing back on the assumption that X was different. Sibling lanes grant a case that is already real as an extreme example (部長にしたって), suppose a case that has not come about (手伝うにしたって), or sweep in every case after an interrogative (誰にしたって).

examples.ruby: 親[おや]にしたって、心配[しんぱい]だから言[い]っているんだよ。
examples.english: My parents, for their part, only say it because they're worried.

examples.ruby: 機械[きかい]にしたって、休[やす]ませなきゃいつかは壊[こわ]れる。
examples.english: A machine too will give out eventually if you never let it rest.

examples.ruby: 私[わたし]にしたって、同[おな]じ立場[たちば]なら断[ことわ]れなかったよ。
examples.english: I couldn't have refused either, in the same position.

glosses: even X; X is no exception
patterns.usage_note: Raises a noun as a case and says that what holds elsewhere holds for it too (新人にしろ, 大手の企業にしろ), typically the very case the listener assumed would be different. Sibling entries concede a supposition that has not come about (引っ越すにしろ) or something already established (断られたにしろ). It attaches to a noun here, not a clause; にしても is the ordinary-register form of this same use.

examples.ruby: 新人[しんじん]にしろ、この程度[ていど]の確認[かくにん]は怠[おこた]るべきでない。
examples.english: Newcomers are no exception: a check this basic shouldn't be skipped.

examples.ruby: 大手[おおて]の企業[きぎょう]にしろ、人手[ひとで]不足[ぶそく]とは無縁[むえん]ではない。
examples.english: Even the big firms are no exception to the labor shortage.

examples.ruby: 大人[おとな]にしろ、慣[な]れない場所[ばしょ]では緊張[きんちょう]する。
examples.english: Adults are no exception; unfamiliar places make them tense too.
